case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment's caption, including the Uttarakhand renaming.

number_of_accused.reason: Seven accused are named and the Court decides all seven appeals.

accused_gender.reason: All accused are described as male through pronouns such as 'his father' and 'his knife'.

accused_age.reason: No accused age is stated anywhere in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: No accused occupation is stated; a shop reference concerns a father, not an occupation of the accused.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class appears.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No accused's criminal record is mentioned; the 'other murder case' concerns witness P.W.3.

victim_gender.reason: The victim Alok Chandana is referred to with male pronouns and is male.

victim_age.reason: The victim's age is not stated.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Acquaintance / fellow college election contestants; accused sought the victim's withdrawal from a college election
accused_victim_relationship.quote: asked Vipin Singh Singh Negi and Alok Chandana to withdraw their names from the election of Commerce faculty of the College
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment describes a college election dispute, not a 'political rival' relationship; 'prior dispute' overstates it.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 IPC, with the case converted to s.302.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302 read with s.149; IPC s.148; additional charges IPC s.147 and s.323 read with s.149; s.307 in the original FIR
statutory_provisions.quote: Charges were framed against all the accused persons under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 of I.P.C. An additional charge was framed ... under Sections 147 and 323 read with Section 149
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits s.147 and s.323 r/w s.149 additional charges and the original s.307 in the FIR.

weapon.reason: Lathis, knives, khukris and danda are all described as weapons used.

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical and recovery evidence are all discussed in the judgment.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by any accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Court notes armed accused and four accused chasing and injuring the deceased after he fell.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted by the Court.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.149 (life imprisonment, Rs.10,000 fine each) and under s.148 (two years RI); sentences concurrent
trial_court_outcome.quote: All the accused persons were also convicted under Section 148 of I.P.C. and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for two years.
trial_court_outcome.reason: Value wrongly applies life sentence to s.148; s.148 carried two years rigorous imprisonment.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeals, affirmed conviction and sentence, and cancelled bail.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeals, upholding the convictions.

offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions under s.302 r/w s.149 and s.148 are upheld; the paraphrase of s.148 is acceptable.

imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment was imposed and upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life sentence is not a fixed term, so null is appropriate.

fine_rs.reason: Rs.10,000 fine on each accused is stated.

neutral_facts.reason: Summary covers incident, investigation and evidence without names, court proceedings or outcome.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment prescribed for s.302.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: Homicidal death with fractured frontal bone and ruptured lung; head laceration from danda on the second student.

number_of_offences.reason: Four sections (147, 148, 302, 323) were charged; ss.302 r/w 149 and 148 were upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or financial loss is involved.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court held the intention to kill may have arisen on the spur of the moment, not planned.

motive.reason: Court accepted the common object of stopping the deceased from contesting the college elections.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Eyewitness testimony of P.W.1 and P.W.3 on presence and roles of all seven accused; medical evidence of injuries and death
key_evidence_accepted.quote: the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses have been fully corroborated by the medical reports of the doctors
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court did not rely on the recovered shirt; it treated the late recovery as an investigation flaw.

witness_credibility.reason: Court found P.W.1 and others reliable, with FIR inconsistencies explained by trauma and no improvement.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No post-offence conduct of the accused is recorded.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of custody is not stated.

bail_history.reason: High Court cancelled the appellants' bail; no other bail history is given.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date and High Court date are given; trial and Supreme Court dates are not.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for appellants and respondent State are listed as in the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: FIR registration, charge sheet and trial completion are described.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Court noted weapon non-recovery and late shirt recovery as flaws, held not fatal.

appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial court, High Court and Supreme Court match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: The judgment does not record prosecution arguments before the Supreme Court.

defence_argument.reason: Listed defence points, including FIR omission, P.W.3 unreliability and no weapon recovery, all appear in the judgment.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Spur-of-moment common object, injured witness credence, minor discrepancies and non-recovery principles are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Dharmendrasinh, Manjit Singh and Ramachandran are the cases relied on, with matching citations.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The Supreme Court gives no sentencing rationale; it only upholds the sentence.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The Court weighs no mitigating factors.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court does not expressly weigh aggravating factors for sentencing.

other_sentence_order.reason: No Supreme Court order beyond dismissal; trial court ordered concurrent sentences, as stated.
